examples.label: Optional parts
examples.purpose: Three optional symbols in a row: FIRST of the sequence reads past each of them, and FOLLOW flows in from the left side.

examples.label: Nullable chain
examples.purpose: Nullability needs one round per level when the rules are listed top-down: the fixpoint is reached late.

examples.label: Balanced parentheses
examples.purpose: A single nullable nonterminal around itself: FOLLOW(S) gets ) from inside and $ from the start.

examples.label: Arithmetic (LL(1) form)
examples.purpose: The textbook sets for the expression grammar with the left recursion removed: FOLLOW(E′) flows down to FOLLOW(T′).

examples.label: Arithmetic (left-recursive)
examples.purpose: FIRST(E) is fed by FIRST(T) and by E itself: left recursion puts cycles in the dependencies.

examples.label: Rules in reverse order
examples.purpose: The sets of the LL(1) form with the rules listed bottom-up: FIRST needs two rounds instead of four.

examples.label: Sentences
examples.purpose: A grammar without ε: FIRST comes from the first symbol of each rule, FOLLOW from the symbol after.

examples.label: Pascal excerpt (declarations)
examples.purpose: Declaration lists with nullable parts: many nullable symbols and long FOLLOW chains.
